concepts.title: Scarcity as Manufactured Value
concepts.description: Duveen buying whole collections into his basement to hold the price. *"You can get all the pictures you want at fifty thousand dollars apiece—that's easy. But to get pictures at a quarter of a million apiece—that wants doing!"* — the price is the product. **The chapter fuses three different scarcities** with different durabilities: natural (nobody can add Vermeers), withheld (Duveen's basement, durable only while he holds), and manufactured desire (the tulip account, least durable of all because a belief cannot be stored in a basement). ⚠ **Greene's instruction to *extend the law to your own skills* drops both of the case's preconditions** — Duveen owned the supply and faced a closed substitute set — and misses that a *finished work* survives a basement while a *practised capacity* degrades in one. **The real move was not becoming scarce; it was buying the substitutes.** ⚠ `[CONTESTED]` on the tulipomania framing: attributing the episode to deliberate engineering by the Dutch upper classes is a strong causal claim, uncited, standing against the general shape of the historical literature. Do not use in output without checking

concepts.title: Duveen and the Elevator at Claridge's
concepts.description: several years of tracking a man who had refused to meet him, household staff on his own payroll, a suite booked directly below Mellon's, and a valet chain executing inside a sixty-second corridor window. **The apparatus had to be standing and idle before the opportunity existed** — the skill on display is not opportunism but tolerance for carrying an expensive machine through long periods when it returns nothing, and nearly all the intelligence collected was correctly wasted. **What the spying bought was not leverage but charm**: *"your knowledge of your mark can also make you seem charming, so well can you anticipate his desires."* Mellon experienced it as being understood, and there is no felt difference between a man who knows you because he loves you and one who knows you because he bought your valet. The larger yield was competitive — rivals found Duveen *"there before him, as if he had a sixth sense"* and withdrew from the category, because an advantage that looks like a *faculty* invites resignation rather than imitation. ⚠ Flags the scope condition Greene never states, supplied by his own Henry Ford counter-case one law later: the method maps desires that already exist and returns nothing where none do

concepts.title: Gould and Lord Gordon-Gordon
concepts.description: **the chapter's most important case and the one that refutes its own definition.** Greene defines deception as *distraction*; this ran for years with no misdirection at any point. Gordon-Gordon's opening gift was *real* — handwriting experts, paid for out of his own pocket, who correctly proved the Erie forgeries were an inside job — which is why it could not later be exposed as fraudulent. **The mechanism is a prior, not a distraction**: *"there had been many clues before then… it took the loss of millions for him to see through the scheme."* Gould was professionally paranoid and saw the evidence; the classification had been set before the evidence existed, so each clue arrived as an anomaly. **Vigilance is therefore the wrong defence** — it operates downstream of classification. The only countermeasure the case supports is periodically re-deriving your view of a person from scratch. ⚠ Also notes the entry timing: arriving mid-crisis, when the gift is worth most and examined least; and that Gould ran the identical mechanism *as operator* at Law 3, uncross-referenced

concepts.title: Harry Cohn and the Chain of Dependence
concepts.description: 1951, HUAC at its height. A die-hard Republican who had visited Mussolini and kept his photograph on the wall refuses to fire a blacklisted communist screenwriter. Not principle, and not merit — *"there were many good writers in Hollywood."* **Lawson was Bogart's writer and Bogart was Columbia's star.** Greene closes off both comfortable readings explicitly, which isolates the chain as the only operating variable. **Indispensability is transitive, and the borrowed form is the only route in the chapter with no entry cost — and the only one you cannot maintain**, since Lawson could do nothing to keep Bogart a star. ⚠ Chronology flagged for checking: Lawson was one of the Hollywood Ten, convicted of contempt in 1948 and imprisoned in 1950, context Greene omits

concepts.title: The Monopoly Trap
concepts.description: the Reversal, opening with the concession the chapter had been avoiding: *"the weakness of making others depend on you is that you are in some measure dependent on them."* Three failure modes — isolation, internal pressure, and **coalition**, which is a *manufacturing* process: a monopolist gives scattered, mutually hostile parties the one thing they have in common. **Independence and dependence are two ways of allocating structural load**, and the monopolist bears all of it — the same fact as Tolstoy's front horse carrying two loads. ⚠ Flags that Morgan and Rockefeller are named as illustrations of a *"ruinous and fruitless"* drive and neither was ruined, and that the closing promise the master *"will in essence be your slave"* reinstates the ambition the Reversal just diagnosed as fatal
